mechanism_principle.content: The equivalence between the proposed expression and the spectral function depends on preparing a state that is an eigenstate of the time-evolution operator; Trotter error breaks this condition.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The equivalence between our approach (5) and the spectral function (2) crucially relies on the fact that the state prepared |E⟩is an eigenstate of the time evolution operator eitH. If this is not the case, for example because of Trotter error when implementing eitH on a digital quantum computer, then (5) and (2) will differ.

mechanism_principle.content: Their quantity remains positive because it is an expectation value of the occupation operator n(k), which only takes values 0 or 1, even when the prepared state is not an exact eigenstate due to Trotter error.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: On the other hand, the quantity (5) is always positive, because it is the expectation value of n(k) = c†(k)c(k) which takes value 0 or 1, and that is 0 when ϵ = 0. This holds true even if the state prepared |E⟩is not an exact eigenstate of the time evolution operator due to Trotter error.

mechanism_principle.content: The recursion issue arises because, under Jordan-Wigner ordering, the relevant fermionic modes are not adjacent, so the same fermionic operations do not map to the same qubit operations as in the original FFT.

mechanism_principle.content: Because the modes are fermionic, the required swaps must be fermionic swaps, implemented by adding CZ gates when adjacent modes are swapped.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Since the modes are fermionic, these swaps must be “fermionic swaps”. This cor- responds to adding a CZj,j+1 operation whenever two adja- cent modes j, j +1 are swapped.

causal_claim.content: Although the method doubles qubits and adds two-qubit-gate overhead, the O(N) shot reduction provides a crucial runtime advantage; without the method, obtaining the same spectral-function color plot would be about 11× more expensive and likely difficult to implement, and this cost advantage grows with system size and dimensionality.

Although the method requires to double the number of qubits and comes with a two-qubit gate over- head due to environment interactions and need for fermionic Fourier transform, the sparing of a factor O(N) in the num- ber of shots provides a crucial runtime improvement for ion- trap quantum computers, where shot time is comparatively slow.
